title: Selective Service chief: Russians moving agents through Orthodox churches
place_text: Selective Service headquarters, New York City

tellings.quote: he says the Russians have been moving agents into the United States through the Orthodox churches
The other church was the one on 97th Street and Fifth and that was the Russian church that owed allegiance to Moscow. That's the one they were running agents through.
tellings.difference: Names the specific church at 97th Street and Fifth Avenue, loyal to Moscow, and tells it firsthand rather than from the Selective Service chief.
tellings.link_reason: This tells the same claim as telling 1, that Russian agents were run through an Orthodox church, now pinned to the Moscow-aligned church.

plain: In 1968, the head of the Selective Service, the military draft office, in New York told the writer Peter Levenda that "the Russians have been moving agents into the United States through the Orthodox churches." Levenda tells Michels this as something he heard directly, and he adds himself that the church in question was the Russian church at 97th Street and Fifth Avenue, the one loyal to Moscow. If true, it would mean Soviet spies were using a Manhattan church as cover.
